entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Chinese military strategist (c. 544–496 BCE) traditionally credited as author of The Art of War, the most influential treatise on military strategy and tactics ever written. His principles — "know your enemy and know yourself" — have been applied to warfare, business, and diplomacy for over 2,500 years.
